headline: The ETS revision names eight sectors and reaches eleven — aluminium, cement and power are covered without being named once
body:
Read row by row, the ETS revision names eight of the register's fourteen sectors in its own text: aviation, construction, carbon capture, chemicals, clean tech, shipping, steel and waste. Counting the sectors its provisions actually reach brings the total to eleven. The three that appear only in the reach column — aluminium, cement and power — are never named by any provision in the file.

They arrive through free allocation. The CBAM factor schedule shrinks free allocation for producers of CBAM-covered goods on a fixed annual path, and does the same automatically for any product category later added to the CBAM goods list. Neither provision lists an industry: it inherits one from the CBAM goods annex, which is where aluminium, cement and power enter.

The practical consequence is that a search of the ETS text for your sector's name is not a test of whether the ETS revision applies to you.

evidence.notes: The two counts are taken across every row in data/ets.json: eight distinct slugs appear in sectors_named, and eleven distinct slugs appear across sectors_named and sectors_reached together. CBAM-01 and CBAM-02 are the only two rows in the file that carry a reached sector without naming one; MST-02 and FND-08 are shown as the contrast, naming six sectors each.
